newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Protel sees $110 mln investment in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Protel sees $110 mln investment in 5 yrs.

text.p: Mexican long-distance telephone operator Protel has earmarked $110 million to invest over the next five years in infrastructure and laying fiber-optic cables, the company's CEO said on Tuesday.
"Total investment planned for the first phase is $110 million, with $50 million during the first year," Protel chief executive officer Benigno Perez Lizaur said at a news conference.
Protel is the long-distance arm of Grupo Comunicaciones San Luis, which has a share of approximately 27 percent of the market for trunking (mobile radio telephony) in Mexico.
One of Protel's partners is Nextel Communications Inc.
Perez said Protel had begun to lay a network of over 1,000 miles of fiber-optic cables with a view to covering 36 cities in Mexico during 1997.
Protel expected to have a three percent share of the long-distance telephone market over the next three years, Perez added.
Mexico's long distance telephone market will be opened to competition on January 1, 1997.
